locations.name: The American Museum of Natural History
locations.prompt: The American Museum of Natural History
locations.factShort: Its blue whale hangs from the ceiling at ninety-four feet, modelled in 1969 from a carcass photographed off South America because nobody had measured a living one. The dinosaur halls hold the largest fossil collection anywhere.

locations.name: The Williamsburg Bridge
locations.factShort: When it opened in 1903 it took the longest-suspension-span title from the Brooklyn Bridge, and it was built cheap and steel-heavy rather than beautiful. It carried so many Lower East Side families across that it was nicknamed the Jews' Highway.

locations.name: The Ridgewood Reservoir
locations.factShort: Drained in 1989 after a century supplying Brooklyn with water, its three empty basins were left alone and grew into genuine forest and wetland inside the city. Birders now record over 130 species in it.

locations.name: The High Bridge
locations.factShort: The oldest surviving bridge in New York, built in 1848 to carry Croton water into Manhattan on Roman-style stone arches. Closed for over forty years, it reopened as a footbridge in 2015.

locations.name: The Garibaldi-Meucci Museum
locations.factShort: Antonio Meucci, who demonstrated a working telephone years before Bell's patent, sheltered Giuseppe Garibaldi here between Italian revolutions. Garibaldi worked in Meucci's candle factory while waiting to go back and unify Italy.
